---
title: "📓 Tutorial"
---

The tutorial has three parts: a small example to play with and visualise transmission, a larger example with more realistic parameter values, and the command-line scripts to run the pipeline yourself.

## Small example

A small simulation, quick to run and easy to look at: 3 hosts (`--Nh`) for 10 generations (`--T`), with 2 parasites passed on per mosquito bite (`--K`), a superinfection probability of 0.18 (`--chi`) and 1 oocyst per mosquito (`--C`).

The Jupyter notebook runs every `krsim` command on this example and looks at what each one writes. Change the parameters to see how transmission changes. With the `krsim` environment active ([Installation](installation.qmd)), run the commands below. The first saves the notebook into your current folder and the second opens it in Jupyter:

```bash
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrc-ide/KR_simulator/main/notebooks/tutorial.ipynb
jupyter notebook tutorial.ipynb
```

The notebook writes its files to `output/` next to it.

### Visualise transmission

The notebook also draws two interactive maps of the true pedigree. These are the maps from this example (seed 123); both are interactive, so you can try them here.

#### Strain transmission map

Who infected whom, generation by generation: founders at the top, current strains at the bottom, one lane per host. Click a strain to highlight its ancestors and descendants. [Open full screen](maps/strain_transmission_map_123.html){target="_blank"}

<iframe src="maps/strain_transmission_map_123.html" width="100%" height="650" style="border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 4px;"></iframe>

#### Pairwise strain pedigree map

Pick two current strains and trace each one's ancestry back through the pedigree. Where the two lineages meet are their shared ancestors. [Open full screen](maps/pairwise_strain_pedigree_map_123.html){target="_blank"}

## Command-line scripts

With the `krsim` environment active, run the five main stages of the small example from a terminal. Results go to `krsim_tutorial_output/` in the current folder (krsim creates it):

```bash
OUT=krsim_tutorial_output

krsim simulate   --Nh 3 --T 10 --K 2 --chi 0.18 --C 1 --random_seed 123 --output_dir $OUT
krsim mutate     --ts $OUT/ts_123.trees --random_seed 123 --output_dir $OUT
krsim coal-mut   --ts $OUT/ts_mut_123.trees --random_seed 123 --output_dir $OUT
krsim vcf-strain --ts $OUT/ts_mut_123.trees --random_seed 123 --output_dir $OUT
krsim vcf-host   --strain_vcf $OUT/output_123_strain.vcf --ind_node_map_csv $OUT/sim_ind_node_map_123.csv \
                 --depth 10 --random_seed 123 --output_dir $OUT
```

Each command prints the files it wrote. Every file name ends in the random seed (`123` here), and every command adds a record of what it ran to `KR_sim_123.log`.

| Command | Reads | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| `simulate` | — | `ts_123.trees`, `sim_ind_node_map_123.csv` |
| `mutate` | `ts_123.trees` | `ts_mut_123.trees` |
| `coal-mut` | `ts_mut_123.trees` | `coal_T_123.csv`, `mut_T_123.csv` |
| `vcf-strain` | `ts_mut_123.trees` | `output_123_strain.vcf` |
| `vcf-host` | `output_123_strain.vcf`, `sim_ind_node_map_123.csv` | `output_123_host.vcf` |

See the [command-line reference](commands.qmd) for every option.
